The core insight of this research lies in treating fantasy football trades as large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. The boom-bust ratio provides a probabilistic descriptor of player volatility, which is essential for risk-adjusted valuation. Opportunity cost valuation introduces a nuanced cost metric that considers not just absolute value but also the forgone utility of alternative roster choices. The knapsack formulation allows for constructing trade packages that maximize value while respecting budget constraints. These primitives form a coherent mathematical framework for scalable trade generation. Dualities emerge between player selection and team pairing strategies—team dissimilarity ensures diversity in proposed trades. Failure modes include overfitting to historical data, misalignment of personalization weights, and insufficient coverage of rare events like injury impacts. The system must balance exploration and exploitation in trade space, especially when scaling to millions of users.
